title: HyperNova Systems x Redwood - Partner discovery call
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and HyperNova Systems to explore GPU/cloud partnership for dedicated inference capacity and co-selling. Covered HyperNova's hardware offerings, integration touchpoints (APIs, billing, networking), security concerns (VPC, KMS), and next steps for benchmarks and contract discussions.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Brooks (Redwood Solutions), Mark Saunders (HyperNova CTO), Elena Ruiz (HyperNova Head of Cloud), Dmitri Kozlov (HyperNova Infra Lead), Priya Nair (HyperNova Partnerships)

Summary: Partner intro / discovery - exploring reseller + integration, focused on Dedicated GPU pools, private deployments, networking and security, and a benchmark plan.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making the time. I'm Ava, I'm the AE on the Redwood side, with Samir our SE. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Mark Saunders: Hey, Mark here, CTO at HyperNova. We're excited to explore how we might partner to resell dedicated GPU capacity and maybe bundle our hardware with Redwood's runtime.
[00:20] Elena Ruiz: Elena, Head of Cloud. I'll be primary for integration and networking questions.
[00:26] Samir Patel: Thanks, Elena. Quick agenda - we'll do intros, get a sense of HyperNova's product & go-to-market, dig into integration patterns (APIs, VPC, peering, billing), and then talk benchmarks and next steps. Sound good?
[00:38] Dmitri Kozlov: Yep, makes sense.
[00:40] Priya Nair: Priya here, I'll be focused on the partnership ops side.
[00:43] Ava Chen: Cool. Mark, can you kick off with a quick overview of HyperNova's stack?
[00:47] Mark Saunders: Sure. So HyperNova we build compute appliances - rack-scale GPU pods targeted at cloud edge and colo. Latest box is the HNV-3 with 8x top-bin accelerators, custom NVLink mesh, cooling optimizations. Our sweet spot is lower-latency regional deployments, and we do both direct sell and channel.
[01:10] Elena Ruiz: We also provide a management plane and a control API for provisioning, and we can expose VPC peering or private ethernet to partners. On security, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in the control plane.
[01:24] Samir Patel: Nice - that maps well to some of Redwood's Private deployment modes. We have three delivery modes - hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For a partner scenario you're describing, most teams start with Dedicated pools we operate for them but co-located in partner data centers or via peering.
[01:48] Mark Saunders: That could work - curious about the contract/commit model. Are you doing monthly reserved capacity? How do you handle overage?
[01:56] Ava Chen: Typically we do reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits, with burst pricing for overage. We can co-design pricing for partner-resold capacity. We'll share a draft pricing sheet after this call.
[02:10] Elena Ruiz: On networking - we need to understand the traffic patterns. Do you expect high egress for embeddings? Any recommendations on VLANs or peering?
[02:20] Samir Patel: Good question. It depends - embeddings can be heavy. We instrument token-level costs and can provide batching and caching to reduce egress. For network, VPC peering or private interconnect is recommended; we can support direct-dns and private endpoints. Small caveat: if you're doing on-prem control plane, audit log forwarding and metrics hook-ups need some setup.
[02:44] Mark Saunders: On the runtime side, are you doing quantization support and which models are validated?
[02:49] Samir Patel: We publish a model catalog with verified performance profiles. We support quantized variants and kernel selection. For partner deployments we usually work with you to validate the HNV-3 topology and tweak kernel schedules - sometimes transcriptions show "KV cash" instead of KV cache - ha, it's a funny transcribe error we saw in earlier calls - but yeah, KV cache tuning is important.
[03:15] Dmitri Kozlov: Right, so for peak QPS what should we size for? Our customers run mixed workloads - chat generation at low latency and batch embeddings.
[03:24] Samir Patel: We'll want traces - actual seq lengths, tokens/sec, and concurrency targets. As a rule of thumb, for low-latency chat you'd want dedicated pools with GPU-bound latency SLOs; for embeddings, batching is more efficient. We'll put together a test matrix.
[03:38] Priya Nair: From a partnership perspective, what's the GTM? Co-sell? Resell? White-label?
[03:44] Ava Chen: All options are possible. Common patterns are: co-sell (introductions + joint demos), reseller (partner bills for capacity and we provide runtime licensing), or referral. We can map commercial terms once we agree on capacity and SLAs.
[03:58] Elena Ruiz: Compliance - SOC 2 and encryption. We need to know if Redwood can support customer-managed KMS and provide audit logs to our control plane.
[04:06] Samir Patel: Yes, we support KMS integrations and can forward audit logs. For Private deployments we can install a private control plane that talks to your KMS/HSM. We'll share our security pack (SOC 2, pen test summaries) after the call.
[04:22] Mark Saunders: Great. Can you run a quick sketch of a benchmark plan - sample workloads and metrics?
[04:27] Samir Patel: Sure. We'll propose: 1) Latency SLO tests for chat (p95 / p99), 2) Throughput for embeddings with batching, 3) Cost per 1M tokens/embedding units, and 4) Failure/fallback tests to simulate load and region failover. We'll need a week of traces and a small pilot (1-2 month) to validate.
[04:47] Elena Ruiz: On the pilot, what's required from our side for network and security?
[04:51] Samir Patel: VPC peering or private interconnect, IAM for a service account, and a few sample datasets. If it's on-prem, some admin access to the management network for the control plane install. We'll send an infra checklist.
[05:05] Ava Chen: For commercial, I'll draft a pricing estimate for 3 capacity tiers and propose a commission structure for reselling.
[05:12] Mark Saunders: Cool. Any specific compatibility concerns with our NVLink mesh or custom rom on the HNV-3?
[05:19] Samir Patel: Usually it's kernel tuning and ensuring the CUDA / driver stack is aligned. We often do a quick smoke test and small perf tuning pass. We'll list driver versions and recommended configs in the infra checklist.
[05:32] Elena Ruiz: One question - will Redwood route requests for cost reasons? Like if capacity is low, will you fall back to hosted variants in other regions? We need to be clear about data residency.
[05:42] Samir Patel: Good point. We have smart routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region constraints. For partner deals where data residency is required, we can pin requests to the partner region and disable cross-region fallbacks. We'll include that as a configuration option.
[05:59] Mark Saunders: Pricing and revenue split matters to our business case. Priya, can you capture what you need?
[06:04] Priya Nair: Yes - we'll need cost of goods (per-GPU/hr), suggested MSRP tiers, and a partner discount schedule. Also, if there are SLA credits or uptime guarantees.
[06:13] Ava Chen: We'll draft all of that.
[06:15] [10:12] Samir Patel: (later in call) digging into technical deep dive - on KV cache sizing, we often see customers misconfigure and lose warm-start benefits. We recommend a shared KV cache policy for similar prompt sets. Any concerns?
[10:28] Dmitri Kozlov: Our ops are used to distributed KV stores; we need memory sizing guidance.
[10:33] Samir Patel: We'll provide a memory sizing table based on model family and typical sequence lengths.
[15:05] Elena Ruiz: About monitoring - can Redwood ship metrics to our Prometheus / Grafana stack?
[15:12] Samir Patel: Yes, we have hooks and can push metrics, traces, and per-route latency. We can also provide long-term retention as an add-on.
[22:40] Mark Saunders: For the benchmark pilot, what should success look like?
[22:45] Samir Patel: Success criteria: meeting p95 latency target for chat under target concurrency, embedding throughput within 10% of baseline, and cost per request within agreed threshold. Also validate failover and monitoring integrations.
[30:01] Ava Chen: OK let's recap next steps - Samir will own the benchmark plan and infra checklist, Ava will send pricing and partner commercial template, HyperNova (Elena) will share traces, and Priya will coordinate internal approvals.
[30:18] Elena Ruiz: Sounds good. Couple of small follow-ups - can you also include model quantization guidance and the list of verified models (we saw the Redwood catalog references earlier)?
[30:27] Samir Patel: Yep, we'll include the catalog link and quantization profiles.
[30:33] Mark Saunders: Any blockers we foresee?
[30:36] Samir Patel: Mainly time to run pilot and legal/commercial negotiation. Nothing technical we can't manage in the pilot.
[30:45] Ava Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send notes and items within a few days.
[58:00] Call end.
